sources.entry: Saywing - Open-source tool that reads selected screen regions aloud using local OCR and neural speech, with offline English and German dictation. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/ChrBoebel/saywing) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Saywing
summary.one_liner: A Mac app that reads selected screen regions aloud and provides dictation, with text recognition, speech, and dictation running locally on the Mac.
use_cases: Reading selected screen regions aloud on a Mac
Dictating text into other apps offline
Listening to text from documents or web pages that cannot be selected
Offline English or German voice dictation
Accessibility support as a supplement to VoiceOver
summary.what_it_does: Saywing reads selected regions of the Mac screen aloud, using local text recognition (OCR) and a neural speech model (Supertonic 3). It also provides dictation using the Whisper Turbo model, with English and German support mentioned on the listing. Text recognition, reading and dictation run locally on the device, and additional dictation models download only after explicit user confirmation. Dictation can insert text into other apps when Accessibility permission is granted. The app includes an update checker that lets the user choose when to install, and update checks do not send screenshots, text or recordings.
notable: Local OCR and neural speech, with no screen content sent off the device
Dictation inserts text into other apps via Accessibility permission
Source code published for the 0.1.17 betas
Listed as open-source and freeware in awesome-mac
caveats: Currently in beta (version 0.1.32); Intel build has only been tested under Rosetta
Reading voice is subject to Open RAIL-M model license use restrictions
Not a complete replacement for VoiceOver; requires Screen Recording and Microphone permissions
